chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Musabbih, from Mandal ibn 'Ali, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed the obligatory prayer while mounted on his beast on a rainy day.'

From him, from al-Himyari, who said: 'I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'May Allah make me your ransom, the mawlas of your forefathers narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed the obligatory prayer while mounted on his beast on a rainy day. Rain falls upon us while we are in our mounts, the ground is wet, and the rain causes discomfort. Is it permissible for us, O Master, to pray the obligatory prayer in this state while in our mounts or upon our beasts, if Allah wills?'
He (peace be upon him) wrote back: 'That is permissible with severe necessity.'

key_terms.فَوَقَّعَ: He wrote back (referring to the Imam's written reply)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray obligatory prayers while riding in a car or on a beast during heavy rain?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the Prophet’s voluntary practice of praying on his mount during rain and the permissibility for others to do so only under conditions of 'severe necessity' (al-ḍarūrah al-shadīdah). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextualizing prophetic precedents to derive specific legal rulings for the community during travel or inclement weather.
